demo.banner: Demo mode. All candidates are fictional.

landing.lead: HRmit is an applicant tracking system that runs on your own computer. Candidates, CVs and notes live in a local database. An AI assistant summarizes CVs and proposes interview questions, but every decision stays with you.

local.title: Local by default
local.text: One command, a panel on localhost, a folder you can back up. Cloud AI is opt-in, bring your own key, and only ever sees anonymized text.

assist.title: AI assists, never judges
assist.text: Summaries, competencies and structured interview questions. No scores, no rankings, no verdicts. The hire is always a human click.

fair.title: Built for fairer hiring
fair.text: Blind screening hides names and contact details. Every candidate for a job gets the same questions and the same criteria.

demo.title: How the demo works
demo.text: The demo is the real app built with one flag: a service worker in your browser answers every API call from fictional fixtures and keeps your changes in localStorage. Nothing is sent anywhere. "Reset demo" in the banner restores the fixtures. AI answers are pre-recorded.

run.title: Run it locally
run.text: Node 24 and pnpm. AI features need Ollama (free, local); see the README for cloud providers and Docker.

prompts.title: Prompts
prompts.intro: The instruction the model gets before the data (job, CV, your question). The shipped texts keep the HRmit rule: describe, never judge, rank or score. If you change them, what the model does is your call and your responsibility. The structured outputs still have no score or verdict field.

backup.title: Backup & Recovery
backup.intro: Download a copy of everything HRmit stores on this computer and keep it somewhere safe. The file contains personal data of your candidates.
backup.demoIntro: Demo mode: the backup is the demo data of this browser as a JSON file. The real app downloads the database and the CV files as one archive.
backup.contains: The archive holds the database (recruitments, candidates, notes, templates, settings, email history) and the uploaded CV files.
backup.noKey: The encryption key is not included, so the stored AI key and SMTP password stay unreadable; enter them again after a restore.
backup.restore: To restore, use the Recovery section below, or by hand: stop HRmit, put hrmit.db and the uploads folder from the archive into the data folder, and start it again.
backup.recoveryIntro: Pick a backup file you downloaded here. Everything it holds replaces what HRmit has now: the database and the CV files. There is no undo, so download a fresh backup first if in doubt.
backup.demoRecoveryIntro: Demo mode: pick the JSON file you downloaded here. It replaces the demo data of this browser.
backup.restoreConfirm: Replace all current data with the backup? This cannot be undone.
backup.notArchive: This is not an HRmit backup file.
backup.damaged: The database in this backup is damaged.

ai.title: AI assistant

ai.previewTitle: What a cloud provider would receive
ai.previewHint: Left: the extracted CV text. Right: the same text after local anonymization. Local providers get the left version.
ai.heuristic: Heuristic, not named-entity recognition: the structured fields (name, email, phone) and common patterns (emails, phones, URLs, PESEL, birth dates, addresses) are replaced. Names that appear only in the CV body, such as references or former managers, can slip through.

update.title: HRmit updates
update.privacy: Checking asks GitHub for the list of HRmit releases. Nothing about your data is sent.
update.failed: Could not check for updates. Is this computer online?
update.backupHint: The database and CV files are saved to data/backups/ before anything changes.

update.reloadHint: HRmit restarts by itself; this page reloads when the new version is up. Keep it open.
update.restart: Version {{version}} is installed. Stop HRmit and start it again to use it.

refused.not a git checkout: This copy is not a git checkout, so it cannot update itself.
refused.up to date: You already have the newest version.
refused.local changes: HRmit's files have local changes. Commit or discard them first, then update.

update.installer: Download the new installer and run it. It stops HRmit, installs the new version over this one and starts it again; your data in the HRmit folder of your user account stays. For extra safety, download a backup under Backup & Recovery first.
